scope: Assessment of continuous slider editing. Current-source CPU-stage measurements and code review; historical native continuity reports reanalysed, not rerun. No optimized application or bundle delivered.

test_environment.background_load: Not controlled; exploratory stage timings, not a statistically qualified interactive benchmark.

verification.reason: Only a standalone diagnostic and assessment records changed; production application, decoder and bundle untouched.

findings.observation: Completed edit jobs must exactly match the latest draft; any new slider change removes an accepted preview and revokes its presentation work before the central viewer draws. A retained texture prevents blank frames but can remain unchanged throughout a gesture.
findings.consequence: Shorter CPU kernels alone cannot guarantee progress while new drafts arrive. Requested, computing and displayed revisions need separate lifetimes, with monotonic provisional presentation within the same valid interaction.

findings.observation: Photographic edits run CPU pixel/filter loops, clone input and rebuild a complete mip tail. The viewer GPU receives edited pixels for resampling/display, keyed by the new image ID. Ordinary editing selects a <=1024-pixel mip in either Standard or Full; explicit final/output proof selects native input.
findings.engine_scope: Shared downstream of Apple, LibRaw bilinear, LibRaw AHD and TrueRenderer development. The microbenchmark uses synthetic working pixels, so it neither executes nor ranks those decoders.

findings.observation: A changed native RAW WB is a new decode identity. Apple selects full native scale with draft disabled; LibRaw reopens/unpacks/processes; TrueRenderer reads the mosaic and develops it for the new gains. Cached source snapshots do not constitute a retained developed sensor session.
findings.measurement: No new decode or native-WB latency campaign was run.

cpu_stage_profile.input: Generated independently at each mip geometry; no RAW decoding, source photography or catalog access.
cpu_stage_profile.scope: CPU edit-worker stages on synthetic opaque linear Rec.2020 pixels; not UI/GPU/RAW or physical-display latency. Base 3 matches the ordinary <=1024px edit mip for the stated geometry in both preview qualities; bases 4/2 explore size cost only. No quality equivalence between mips is claimed.

historical_continuity_reanalysis.scope: Four engines x CPU/GPU x provisional edit preview/native output proof. This is not Standard/Full and has no 60 Hz input schedule or physical display timestamps.
historical_continuity_reanalysis.result: All 16 traces passed their original coverage criterion yet retained only one displayed image through the 40 moving steps, then showed the final image.

recommended_order: Measure frame freshness; separate requested, computing and displayed revisions. Keep one active job and one replaceable latest pending draft; show monotonic intermediate frames only within a compatible interaction.

Prioritize visible editing over thumbnails/histograms. Prepare coefficients, skip neutral work, use the bounded shared CPU pool where valid, reuse scratch and avoid unneeded mip construction. Measure adaptive interaction resolution.

Resident GPU editing graph shared after all four RAW engines: point operations first, then geometry/spatial filters/masks; qualify every node against CPU before enabling it. Refine selected Standard/Full on gesture release.

Qualify bounded native WB sessions inside XPC workers per engine. Apple filter/scale reuse and LibRaw unpack reuse are candidates, not measured improvements. Account retained memory, cancellations, source epochs and worker recovery.
Validate four engines x two qualities x CPU/GPU with actual slider gestures, final export parity, late-result rejection, memory and XPC where affected.

proposed_interaction_targets.status: Design targets to qualify, not achieved rates. Existing photo-spec command-to-frame targets remain in force.

primary_design_references.supports: Reuse contexts, choose output pixel count and avoid unnecessary CPU/GPU texture transfers. TrueRenderer deliberately bounds large context lifetime today; any reuse must requalify memory. Color management is retained.
CIRAWFilter exposes a smaller output scale as a performance option. TrueRenderer compatibility and fidelity remain to be measured.
LibRaw can retain unpacked state while freeing postprocessing output for another processing call with different settings. A bounded XPC session remains application work to design and test.
Queue writes stage updates until submission; persistent image data with small parameter updates is feasible, with explicit staging and completion lifetimes.

limitations: 20 timed samples per case; no p95/p99 claim. 360 samples plus 36 warmups across 18 cases.
Stage timings exclude UI events, thread launch/wake, presentation, upload, GPU completion, display, RAW decode, cache IO and concurrent thumbnail work.

The 754x504 raster uses native geometry metadata 6032x4032. No 24-megapixel source was decoded. Each tested mip is generated independently; different scales were not compared for photographic equivalence.
Histogram timing is separate and at each tested raster size; production thumbnails use <=512 pixels and their own work.
Historical continuity traces refer to older builds and are not a fresh native or Standard/Full qualification.
No user photography/catalog accessed by the profiler; no bundle replaced; no application speedup, RAW/color/Windows qualification or R/SF gate completion claimed.
